'''Vuvrians''' were a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species with large, twelve-eyed [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] heads, native to the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] known as [[Vurdon Ka/Legends|Vurdon Ka]]. Averaging about two meters tall, Vuvrians were cordial, diplomatic, and inquisitive in nature. As a result of living on an almost idyllic homeworld&mdash;Vurdon Ka was a windless world of mosses and trees, and lacked any predator species&mdash;the species developed extremely sensitive skin, which declined in sensitivity as a Vuvrian aged.

Vuvrians were natural problem solvers. Vuvrian [[Force-sensitive]]s were not uncommon, but they made poor soldiers due to their extremely low pain threshold. Although they were important members of Galactic society, Vuvrians never made any attempts to colonize other worlds, preferring to stay on their peaceful home planet.

==Biology and appearance==
Vuvrians were lightly built, twelve-eyed bipedal insectoid [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]]. They had an oblong-shaped head on top of their long, thin necks. They had twelve eyes, varying in size and color, and two long, thin antennae on their heads. They stood about 2 meters tall, with [[Gender/Legends|females]] displaying slightly thinner builds and more oblong-shaped heads.<ref name="UAA" /> Many other species found the Vuvrians' appearance almost comical.<ref name="GG07">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

As a species, the Vuvrians evolved a highly fine sense of touch, a survival mechanism developed in response to the few predators that called Vurdon Ka home. A Vuvrian's skin was so sensitive that an individual could, for example, feel the minute shifts in air temperature when another being walked into a room. Such heightened sense was often mistaken by other species for latent telepathic ability or even [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitivity. Indeed, a number of Vuvrians excelled as [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], with their innate abilities augmented by the power of the Force. As a Vuvrian aged, however, their skin became increasingly wrinkled and less sensitive&mdash;a process that was accelerated in harsh offworld environments such as those found on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] or [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. Vuvrians did not deal well with pain.<ref name="UAA" />

Considered younglings until they reached eleven standard years old, Vuvrians reached adulthood at around eighteen. Society considered Vuvrians over the age of sixty to be elderly, and anyone over the age of eighty was thought to be venerable, commanding respect due to their old age.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Vuvrian_AA.jpg|thumb|left|170px|A Vuvrian]]
Vuvrians as a species were intelligent and inquisitive in nature. A warm, sincere, friendly people, Vuvrians were very diplomatic, and were natural problem solvers. Although some species found the Vuvrians' physical appearance somewhat disturbing, it was difficult to resist their outgoing, charismatic personality, and their skill in oration and logical argument often meant others found it all but impossible not to see a Vuvrian's point of view. The species' genuine interest in learning about other cultures, and to help others solve problems, ingratiated many Vuvrians into the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and made it easy for a Vuvrian to notice the quirks in other species' cultures.<ref name="UAA" />

Common Vuvrian names included Cimilak, Gwent, Kirrewa, Mylthea, Nilzilun, Scrin, Swiegel and Weelax.<ref name="UAA" />

As well as their [[Vuvrian (language)|own language]], Vuvrians could speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] and read and write [[Aurebesh/Legends|aurebesh]].<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
The Vuvrians never developed a great interest in offworld colonization, despite being long-standing members of galactic society. Rather than found colonies and enclaves outside their home system, Vuvrians were content to tour and observe the greater galaxy, although many found other worlds, and even space stations, paled in comparison to the paradise of Vurdon Ka. Curiously, it was noted that those Vuvrians who settled offworld tended to gravitate towards harsher climates, and xenobiologists were unable to explain why this was so.<ref name="UAA" />

Vuvrians were more than happy to join the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Many of the species' Force-sensitives joined the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="UAA" /> including the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Nystammall]], who was ultimately killed by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="US">{{InsiderCite|86|Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous}}</ref>

Following the Clone Wars, many Vuvrians were employed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to negotiate trade contracts and rare disputes where even the military might of the Imperial regime was not practical or productive. Despite this, many Vuvrians also aided the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], where they proved to be adept spies.<ref name="UAA" />

Other Vuvrians were content to remain neutral during the conflict.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

==Vuvrians in the galaxy==
[[File:Wioslea.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Wioslea/Legends|Wioslea]] on the streets of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]]]

Vuvrians, as natural problem solvers, could often be found in diplomatic or business-related fields, and many of the species became known as some of the greatest sales-beings, negotiators, and first-contact specialists in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Vuvrians scouts and spies were not uncommon, but they made poor soldiers, due to their extreme intolerance to physical pain. Many Vuvrians were employed as law enforcers, as their twelve eyes distributed on all sides of their head gave them omnidirectional vision, which provided a huge advantage in that line of work.<ref name="UAA" />

[[Wioslea/Legends|Wioslea]] was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Vuvrian speeder merchant who resided on [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] during the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. She bought Luke Skywalker's [[X-34 landspeeder/Legends|X-34 landspeeder]] for [[Spaceport Speeders/Legends|Spaceport Speeders]], a local Mos Eisley company that bought and sold landspeeders and other vehicles. Wioslea was also a gambler. Due to outstanding gambling debts, at the time of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Death/Legends|death]], she owed him about 1,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Imperial Credits]]. Wioslea was also able to speak many languages, including [[Arconese/Legends|Arconese]], [[Aqualish (language)/Legends|Aqualish]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Rodese/Legends|Rodese]], [[Sullustese/Legends|Sullustese]], and [[Vregg]].<ref name="GG07" />

Nystammall was a male Vuvrian, who was a member of the Jedi Order during the Clone Wars, with the position of Jedi Master. He was stationed on the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] world of [[Tovarskl]] with his former Master, a four-armed [[Eirrauc]] known as [[Puroth]], during the Clone Wars. It was while stationed there that the two Jedi were [[Battle of Tovarskl|killed]] by General Grievous. The cyborg then took their blue [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] as trophies.<ref name="US" />

==Behind the scenes==
''[[Cantina Communications]]'' makes reference to a species of emotionless, multi-eyed insectoids said to be the best pilots in the galaxy. Though the cultural description is quite different from the Vuvrians, author [[John Chesterman]] may have had the Vuvrians in mind when making this reference.<ref name="CC">{{StoryCite|story=Cantina Communications|book=Star Wars Official Poster Monthly 16}}</ref>
